headline_findings: The treatise key 'iterated2023' is almost certainly Steiner, 'Solving Degree Bounds for Iterated Polynomial Systems' (arXiv:2310.03637, Oct 2023; ToSC 2024(1)). It is the only 2023 paper with an iterated-system lower-bound technique for solving degree: lower bounds on Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity via explicit polynomials with degree falls, valid when few solutions lie in the base field, plus Thm 7.5 'last fall degree = satiety of F^hom in generic coordinates'. The treatise .bib was not found locally so this identification is inferred from the citation context (prog_openproblems.tex line 154), not read from the bib entry.

No 2025-2026 paper on 'first fall degree assumption', 'Semaev Assumption 1', summation-polynomial Weil descent, quasi-subfield polynomials, or WDSat successors from the original authors was found on arXiv or ePrint (searches listed in queries_run). The only 2025-2026 hits on Weil-descent SAT are the programme's own GitHub PRs and one CoDIT 2025 ANF-SAT paper already carded as KN-LIT-92919e.

No 2024-2026 successor to Faugere-Svartz (Groebner bases of ideals invariant under a finite abelian group, non-modular case) was found; the 2025 'equivariant Groebner bases' literature (Ghosh-Lopez 2507.08990) concerns infinite-variable rings and decidability, not finite Frobenius actions over F_2. Lever 5 therefore has no external competitor and no external shortcut: it stays an in-house engineering item.

Lever 1 has one genuinely usable external tool: Huang 2311.02804 (semi-local systems) proves last fall degree <= s + c'*ceil(log2 s) for zero-dimensional Weil-descent systems with radical local ideals, independent of n. This bounds d_F from ABOVE by the number of closed-point solutions s, which for S_{m+1} restricted to subspaces is the number of decompositions over the algebraic closure, generically bounded by deg S_{m+1} and NOT growing with n. Combined with Steiner's degree-fall lower-bound technique it gives a two-sided framework the programme has not exploited: (a) upper bound via s and the local degrees; (b) lower bound via explicit degree-fall polynomials. Caveat: the S_{m+1} descent is NOT zero-dimensional before adding field equations and the local ideals are not obviously radical, so Theorem 3.1 does not apply verbatim; Theorem 3.2 (rational points, with Artin-Schreier/field equations) gives O(Delta p) with p = 2, which is also n-independent but with an unspecified constant.

Macaulay-bound refinements since 2024: Gaggero-Gorla (same-degree systems, v4 Aug 2026, conditional on Eisenbud-Green-Harris; exact d_reg = n(D-1)+1 for m=n and sharp bounds with field equations), Salizzoni (solv.deg <= max{d_reg+1, deg f_i} for degree-compatible orders, optimal), Kudo-Yokoyama (v4 Sep 2026, synchronization of affine/homogenized computations until the first degree fall), Jaques-Ran-Samardjiska-Seitner (fractional 'smoothed' d_reg, ASIACRYPT 2026). All are UPPER bounds assuming (semi-)regularity or genericity; none gives a lower bound tool for structured Weil-descended systems. Only Steiner's degree-fall lemma does.

Boolean solving records 2025-2026: Fukuoka MQ Type I/III/IV have no new entries in 2025-2026 (Bouillaguet-Sauvage n=76 Type I from 2023-06 still stands). New: Type II n=38 (Verbel, XL+BW, 2026-09-28), Type V n=31 (Li-Sun, 'improved F4 via smaller matrices', GPU, 2026-09-17, no paper yet), Type VI n=36 (Sakata-Takagi HDF4+MF4, 2025-10-16). Bouillaguet-Sauvage ePrint 2026/1704 improves Dinur-2 by 1-4 bits for MQOM parameters and attacks PGOW-MQ; Vidal-Delaplace-Ionica 2026/360 corrects the Crossbred complexity analysis. None changes the exponent class the programme already uses (Crossbred 0.891, Dinur 0.6943 for quadratic Boolean).

F4 engineering 2026 within the window: Demin Las-Vegas F4 (2609.14433, 2026-09-13; already KR-IC-0d2021), Kouba-Neiger-Safey El Din F4 Tracer complexity (2603.16378), Lairez-Mohr-Ternier MDD data structure for signature GB (2601.05026 v3), msolve v0.10/v0.11 (improved Gebauer-Moeller, probabilistic linear algebra fixes). Constant-factor only; relevant to making lever-1 cells (m,l)=(4,4),(4,5),(4,6) affordable.

papers.title: Solving Degree Bounds for Iterated Polynomial Systems
papers.summary: Extends Caminata-Gorla's 'generic coordinates => solving degree <= Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity <= Macaulay bound' framework to iterated systems (MiMC, Feistel-MiMC, Hades, GMiMC). Thm 7.5: for systems in generic coordinates the last fall degree equals the satiety of F^hom. Lower bounds: any explicit polynomial f in (F) with a degree fall in degree d gives reg(F^hom) >= d; applied to MiMC under the hypothesis that fewer than three solutions lie in the base field (e.g. q+2r-2 <= reg <= q+2r for MiMC with one field equation). This is the only 2023 paper with an 'iterated-system lower-bound technique' on solving degree and is therefore the probable referent of the treatise key iterated2023 (identification unverified against the bib file).
papers.relevance: Lever 1: the ONLY external lower-bound technique found. Recipe for the programme: (i) check whether the Weil-descended S_{m+1} on an l-dim subspace, with field equations, is in generic coordinates (Caminata-Gorla Def 2.5: x_0 non-zero-divisor mod I^sat; equivalently F^top zero-dimensional with radical (x_1..x_n)) -- the programme's own result that d_F depends on presentation suggests it is NOT, so Thm 7.5 may fail and the satiety route is blocked; (ii) regardless of genericity, an explicit degree-fall polynomial in degree d certifies reg(F^hom) >= d, and the programme's closure certificates (1 notin W_c) are exactly witnesses that no fall occurs below c; the missing step is to exhibit a family of fall polynomials whose degree grows with n or l. Steiner's hypothesis 'few base-field solutions' is natural for PDP instances (0 or 1 decomposition). Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: Cited by the treatise as iterated2023 (prog_openproblems.tex:154) but no literature card for Steiner 2310.03637 exists in crypto-autoresearcher knowledge/literature (grep 'steiner' hits only Michael Steiner).
papers.suggested_route: Experiment (toy, msolve/F_2): for binary S_3/S_4 descents at n=13..25, l=3..6, compute reduced Groebner basis with and without the field equations; test generic coordinates via Caminata-Gorla Thm 3.2 criterion (F^top zero-dimensional?); if not generic, record the gap between satiety of F^hom and measured d_F. Then search the degree-c truncation W_c(F) for explicit fall polynomials (elements of W_c of degree < c that are not in W_{c-1}) and tabulate the maximal fall degree vs n: this is Steiner's lower bound applied to PDP. A fit growing with n kills the subexponential heuristic; a plateau supports f(m).

papers.title: Solving degree, last fall degree, and related invariants
papers.venue: Journal of Symbolic Computation 114 (2023); arXiv:2112.05579; ePrint 2021/1611
papers.summary: Relates solving degree to last fall degree (solv.deg >= last fall degree, with equality conditions for degree-compatible orders) and degree of regularity to Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity; introduces generic coordinates as the genericity condition under which solv.deg <= reg(F^hom) <= Macaulay bound.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: the base framework and the convention the treatise uses for first fall degree; the open question of whether d_F for descended S_{m+1} grows is a question about reg(F^hom) when in generic coordinates, and about satiety otherwise. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Background only; already applied in the treatise (falldegree.tex cites caminata2023 Thm 2.8).

papers.title: The complexity of solving Weil restriction systems
papers.authors: Alessio Caminata, Michela Ceria, Elisa Gorla
papers.summary: Upper bounds for the Groebner complexity of Weil(F) in terms of invariants of F over the extension field; Cor 3.4(1): Weil(F) in generic coordinates over k implies sd(Weil(F)) <= n*reg(F) - n + 1 (linear in the extension degree n).
papers.relevance: Lever 1: the only published bound on Weil-descended solving degree is LINEAR in n (upper bound), consistent with growth; it says nothing about lower bounds and requires generic coordinates for Weil(F), which the programme's presentation-dependence result suggests fails. No 2024-2026 successor from these authors exists (author pages checked: Gorla's 2025-26 papers are coding theory + syndrome decoding; Caminata's are isogeny modelings, CCZ, F4/FGLM tutorial). Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Measure whether Weil(S_{m+1}|_V) with field equations is in generic coordinates at toy n (same experiment as Steiner entry); if yes, the n*reg(F)-n+1 bound is the relevant ceiling and lever 1 reduces to reg(F) over F_{2^n}, a quantity independent of n for fixed m.

papers.title: Last fall degree of semi-local polynomial systems
papers.summary: Defines c-semi-local systems (linear transforms of products of local systems in c-variable blocks). Thm 3.1: if |Z(G)| = s > 0, local ideals radical with last fall degree <= c', then d_G <= s + c'*ceil(log2 s), with no condition on |k| and no dependence on n; all s closed points found in n^{O(c')} + s^{O(c log s)}. Thm 3.2: with Artin-Schreier/field equations over k=F_{p^d}, d_{G u E'} = O(Delta p) when exactly one k-rational solution, O(max(Delta p, s0 p, s0 log s0)) in general. Thm 4.1: the Weil descent of {f_1..f_c} in K[x_1..x_c] (K/k degree n) is c-semi-local, and so is any GL_{cn}(k)-conjugate. Applied to HFE.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: the strongest external statement bearing on 'does d_F grow with n'. For a zero-dimensional Weil-descent system with radical local ideals the last fall degree is bounded by the number of closed points s, which is independent of n. Scope limits: (a) S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m) restricted to V^m has c = 1 per block only after the subspace restriction is built in as a linear substitution, so the descended system IS semi-local by Thm 4.1 but its local ideals (one polynomial in m variables over K) are NOT zero-dimensional and NOT obviously radical, so Thm 3.1 does not apply verbatim; (b) Thm 3.2 adds the field equations (which is exactly the programme's setting) and gives an n-independent bound O(Delta*2) with Delta = max(|Z(F_i)|, d_{F_i}), but the constant is unspecified and |Z(F_i)| over the closure is infinite for positive-dimensional F_i. The theorem therefore supports 'f(m) independent of n' ONLY for a modified zero-dimensional formulation, e.g. after fixing enough variables (hybrid) so that the local system is zero-dimensional. Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: KN-LIT-a2f7b3 exists, but the brief's lever-1 text does not use the semi-local upper bound; the connection to the (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) cells is new.
papers.suggested_route: Experiment: at n=13..21, l=3..5, m=3, make the local system zero-dimensional by adjoining the field equations (x_i^{2^n} - x_i, in descended form) and measure (i) s = number of closed-point solutions of the descended system (msolve over F_2, count via degree of the ideal), (ii) measured d_F. Test Huang's inequality d_F <= s + c' ceil(log2 s) and whether s itself is n-independent. If d_F tracks s and s is bounded by deg S_{m+1}-type quantities, lever 1 resolves toward 'bounded in n' for the zero-dimensional formulation; a violation locates the non-radical/non-zero-dimensional obstruction.

papers.title: An upper bound for the solving degree in terms of the degree of regularity
papers.summary: Proves solv.deg(F) <= max{d_reg(F)+1, deg f_i} for degree-compatible orders when d_reg is finite, shows the bound is optimal, and derives a Macaulay bound and an upper bound on the last fall degree (last fall degree <= d_reg).
papers.relevance: Lever 1: makes d_reg (Hilbert-series computable from the top-degree parts F^top) an upper bound on d_F whenever d_reg is finite, i.e. whenever F^top is zero-dimensional. For descended S_{m+1} with field equations F^top includes the x_i^2 (char 2) so d_reg is finite; the programme's dreg measurements (LEAD-ICE-chained-semaev-dreg-vs-semiregular) are therefore rigorous upper bounds on d_F, not heuristics. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Re-read the programme's measured 'd_reg vs semi-regular null' tables as rigorous d_F upper bounds via Salizzoni; where measured d_F equals d_reg+1 the bound is tight and the Hilbert series of F^top (cheap, no Groebner basis) predicts d_F. Test on the PKM-tower plateau (lever 4): compute d_reg of F^top for t=1..14 and compare with the registered prediction d_F = 4 + floor((t-2)/4).

papers.title: The complexity of solving a system of equations of the same degree
papers.summary: For m >= n equations all of degree D with linearly independent top parts and finite d_reg, conditional on the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture: d_reg <= (D-t) + (n-k)(D-1) with (k,t) determined by m-n (Thm 25; exact d_reg = n(D-1)+1 for m=n, sharp for LPP ideals); Cor 29 solv.deg^m <= D-t+1+(n-k)(D-1). With field equations x_i^q - x_i (Thm 35, q <= D <= n(q-1)): d_reg <= B := q-t+(n-k)(q-1), solv.deg^s <= 2(B-1), solv.deg^m <= B+1; Prop 33: for generic systems with enough equations d_reg = D, solv.deg^s <= 2D-2.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: refines the Macaulay bound for same-degree systems and, with field equations over F_2 (q=2), gives B = 2-t+(n-k), still linear in the number of variables; the 'mutant' solving degree solv.deg^m <= B+1 is the bound relevant to MutantXL-style closure. The descended S_{m+1} systems are NOT same-degree (quadratic field equations + degree-2^{m-1} descended polynomials), so the theorem does not apply directly; a homogenised 'same degree' reformulation (multiply low-degree equations by monomials) is a standard device. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Accounting experiment: compare the Gaggero-Gorla B+1 mutant bound (treating the descended system as degree-D after padding) with measured D at m=3,4 cells; if the bound sits far above the measurement, it confirms the structured systems are far from LPP-extremal and the lever-1 question cannot be settled by generic upper bounds.

papers.title: Degree bounds and synchronization in Gröbner basis computations for affine semi-regular systems (formerly: The solving degrees for computing Gröbner bases of affine semi-regular polynomial sequences)
papers.summary: Two upper bounds on the maximal Groebner-basis degree of the homogenised affine system (via a regular initial subsequence of top parts; via the saturation exponent w.r.t. the homogenising variable). Shows Buchberger-style computations on the affine system, its homogenisation and its top parts synchronise until the first degree fall (= when multiplication by the homogenising variable stops being injective); under cryptographic semi-regularity this holds up to d_reg, giving upper bounds on the algorithmic solving degree from affine input.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: formalises exactly the quantity the programme measures ('closure degree in an F4/MutantXL run from affine input') and shows it is controlled by the first degree fall and the saturation exponent of F^hom w.r.t. x_0; for the descended S_3 with d_ff = 2 the synchronisation breaks at degree 2, so the affine computation diverges from the homogeneous one almost immediately, which is why the programme's d_F is presentation-dependent. The saturation exponent is a computable invariant that could be tabulated vs n as a proxy for d_F growth. Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: KN-LIT-27201d records the 2024 version; v4 (2026-09-01, retitled, with the synchronisation theorem) falls in the 8-week window.
papers.suggested_route: Compute the saturation exponent sat_{x0}(F^hom) of descended S_3/S_4 instances at n=13..25 (msolve: Groebner basis of F^hom, then colon ideals (I : x_0^k) until stable) and compare with measured d_F; Kudo-Yokoyama's second bound says d_F <= max degree bound from sat exponent, so growth of sat exponent with n is a cheap precursor of growth of d_F.

papers.title: On Hilbert-Poincaré series of affine semi-regular polynomial sequences and related Gröbner bases
papers.venue: Mathematical Foundations for Post-Quantum Cryptography (Springer, Mathematics for Industry, 2024); arXiv:2401.07768 (v2 2024-03-03)
papers.summary: Survey of Groebner complexity for overdetermined affine semi-regular sequences plus an explicit formula for the truncated Hilbert-Poincaré series of the homogenisation, used to describe the reduced Groebner bases of the affine ideal and its homogenisation.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: supplies the semi-regular null hypothesis in closed form for the affine (non-homogeneous) case, which is the correct null for the programme's 'd_reg vs semi-regular' comparisons on descended systems with field equations. Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: 10 KB hits on 'kudo'; this specific 2024 chapter not confirmed as carded.
papers.suggested_route: Use the affine truncated Hilbert-Poincaré formula as the null in LEAD-ICE-chained-semaev-dreg-vs-semiregular instead of the homogeneous Bardet-Faugère-Salvy series.

papers.title: Smoothing the degree of regularity for polynomial systems
papers.authors: Samuel Jaques, Lars Ran, Simona Samardjiska, Melvin Seitner
papers.summary: Defines a fractional 'smoothed' degree of regularity by using specific submatrices of the Macaulay matrix between two integer degrees, under an assumption generalising semi-regularity (tested experimentally); smooths XL complexity for MQ and saves a few bits on a UOV attack.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: accounting refinement only (constant/sub-degree factor); irrelevant to growth of d_F. Lever 5: the submatrix idea composes with equivariant blocks (both are row/column selections of the Macaulay matrix) but no exponent effect.
papers.suggested_route: None beyond pricing: if the programme reports XL/Macaulay costs at integer D, the smoothed D could lower stage costs by a few bits at the (4,4)-(4,6) cells; classify as engineering.

papers.title: The Complexity of Algebraic Algorithms for LWE
papers.summary: Proves the Arora-Ge LWE system is in generic coordinates, hence its DRL solving degree is bounded by Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and the Macaulay bound; generalises the Semaev-Tenti Groebner algorithm to any system with finite d_reg; sub-exponential estimates for binary-secret/binary-error LWE; effect of hints.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: methodological template for proving generic coordinates for a structured cryptographic system (the LWE proof uses the shape of the top-degree parts). The same check for descended S_{m+1}|_V has never been done by the programme; Steiner's Ciminion/Hydra paper (2405.05040) also gives a linear-system test for generic coordinates. Also notable: Semaev-Tenti's algorithm (the Semaev lineage) is what gets generalised. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Port the generic-coordinates test (Caminata-Gorla Thm 3.2 / Steiner's linear-system test) to descended S_3, S_4 on random and polynomial subspaces at n=13..33; output a boolean per instance. This decides which of the two lever-1 proof routes (satiety vs non-generic) is open.

papers.title: Symmetric Models for Syndrome Decoding
papers.summary: Models the exact binary syndrome decoding weight constraint by elementary symmetric polynomials e_{n,2^i}(x) = t_i (Lucas' theorem mod 2) with parity checks and field equations; proves d_reg(I_n) = floor(n/2)+1 for the symmetric ideal and dsol(S) <= 2^r (+1) with r = floor(log2 n), via Salizzoni's bound; an instance-dependent variant S' drops the top symmetric equation and gets dsol <= floor((k+rk L)/2)+2. Uses S_n-symmetry of the ideal (membership of one squarefree monomial implies all permutations) to compute Hilbert functions, not as a computational group-action reduction.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: demonstrates a proved exact d_reg for a highly symmetric Boolean ideal with field equations, by combinatorial Hilbert-function counting (Wilson's lemma on inclusion matrices) rather than by Groebner computation -- the kind of argument needed for a rigorous d_F bound on descended systems, whose Frobenius symmetry (Z/n rather than S_n) could play the same role. Lever 5: conceptually adjacent (symmetry used to prove, not to compute); also relevant to open lever 6 (Hamming-ball bases) since e_{n,2^i} are exactly the bounded-degree Hamming-ideal generators behind KN-OPEN-5e3dd0.
papers.suggested_route: Theory experiment: for the Frobenius-folded descended S_3 ideal (Z/n acting by cyclic shift of the F_2 coordinates in a normal basis), attempt to compute the Hilbert function of the Z/n-invariant part degree by degree via orbit counting of squarefree monomials modulo the ideal (as Gorla-Trebiani do with S_n), at n=13..31; compare with the full Hilbert function. If the invariant Hilbert function has a closed form, lever 5's block sizes and lever 1's degree of regularity become provable rather than measured.

papers.title: Hamming Ideals and Gröbner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
papers.authors: Roberto La Scala, Marco Marchesin, Sharwan K. Tiwari
papers.summary: Derives defining equations of the Hamming variety via elementary symmetric functions, then uses convolution identities and Lucas-based factorisations to obtain an equivalent system with auxiliary variables and bounded-degree equations; GBDecode fixes part of an information set and solves the rest with MultiSolve (many small Groebner bases after exhaustive assignment of some variables). Experiments at Classic McEliece Category-1 sizes.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none directly. Lever 6 (not this lane, flagged): gives a bounded-degree presentation of the Hamming-weight constraint with auxiliary variables, which is the ingredient KN-OPEN-5e3dd0 (Hamming-ball factor base with bounded-degree membership) needs for a non-subspace Frobenius-stable base at prime n. Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: KN-LIT-316c94 carded; v3 of 2026-10-28 is in the window.
papers.suggested_route: Hand to the factor-base lane: descend S_3(x_1,x_2,x(R)) with x_i constrained to Hamming weight <= w via the La Scala et al. bounded-degree auxiliary system; measure d_F vs w and n at n=13..21 against the subspace baseline.

papers.title: Probably correct row echelon form in the F4 algorithm
papers.summary: Gives the first bound on the failure probability of the Monagan-Pearce-Steel probabilistic row-echelon trick used in state-of-the-art F4 implementations, and a Las-Vegas F4 variant that experimentally beats deterministic F4 on classical examples.
papers.relevance: Lever 5: engineering enabler for the equivariant F4 (the probabilistic echelon trick applies block-wise to character blocks over F_{2^130}); constant factor only. Lever 1: none.
papers.suggested_route: None; already in KR-IC-0d2021.

papers.title: A complexity analysis of the F4 Gröbner basis algorithm with tracer data
papers.authors: Robin Kouba, Vincent Neiger, Mohab Safey El Din
papers.summary: Under Moreno-Socías' conjecture (generic zero-dimensional case), formalises the 'increasing degree property' of regular sequences, analyses F4 pair selection and gives an exact formula for the number of grevlex basis elements in half the degrees; yields a precise complexity formula for the F4 Tracer (F4 with learned reduction trace, msolve's multi-modular engine) improving prior bounds by a factor exponential in the number of variables.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: it is a generic-case result; the descended systems are far from generic (d_ff = 2), so the formula does not transfer, but it is the right null for 'how much cheaper than generic is the structured system'. Lever 5: the F4 Tracer is the natural host for 'F4 trace reuse across many similar systems' (already a known mechanism in the atlas) and for equivariant blocks: a trace learned once per character block could be replayed across the barrel.
papers.suggested_route: Engineering: measure msolve's tracer replay time vs fresh F4 on 100 descended S_3 instances at n=21, l=4 (same shape, different R); the tracer speedup is the realistic ceiling for 'trace reuse' before any equivariant work.

papers.title: Initial ideals of generic ideals and variations of Moreno-Socías conjecture
papers.summary: Proves the initial ideal of a generic ideal is Borel-fixed for any monomial order (a weakening of Moreno-Socías), gives a stability-condition method to compute initial ideals of generic ideals, relates the lex case to lexsegment ideals (bounding maximal Groebner degree), and poses a lex analogue of the conjecture. No full proof of Moreno-Socías found in 2025-2026.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: Moreno-Socías underlies both the Kouba-Neiger-Safey El Din F4 bound and the Sakata-Takagi leading-monomial algorithm; still conjectural, so all 'generic' solving-degree formulas remain conditional. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: None (background on the conditional status of generic bounds).

papers.title: An Algorithm for Computing the Leading Monomials of a Minimal Gröbner Basis of Generic Sequences
papers.summary: Computes the leading monomials of the minimal grevlex Groebner basis of a generic homogeneous sequence without polynomial reductions, assuming the conjectured weakly-reverse-lexicographic initial ideal (Moreno-Socías) and the known Hilbert series; degree-by-degree construction with divisibility-check pruning; lower time/memory than a full Groebner computation. Companion to the HDF4 (Hilbert-driven F4) engine that set Fukuoka Type VI records on 2025-10-16 (n=34,36 over GF(31), with a 'mutant' MF4 component; TCHES 2026).
papers.relevance: Lever 1: a 'generic leading-monomial skeleton' is exactly the null against which structured descended systems deviate; comparing the actual leading monomials of the descended S_3 basis with the generic skeleton would locate where structure enters (degree 2 by the trace linear equation, then where?). Lever 5: HDF4's Hilbert-driven selection of how many S-pairs to build per degree is directly reusable inside an equivariant F4 (per character block). Engineering class.
papers.novelty_note: HDF4/TCHES 2026 is carded (KN-LIT-c14d68, KR-IC-0d2021); this 2025-26 arXiv companion is not.
papers.suggested_route: Diagnostic: dump the leading-monomial set of the reduced grevlex basis of a descended S_3 instance (msolve) and diff against the generic skeleton of the same (n_vars, degrees) predicted by Sakata-Takagi; the first degree where they differ beyond the trace relation is the structured 'excess' that lever 1 must explain.

papers.title: Fukuoka MQ Challenge: 2025-2026 hall-of-fame entries (Type II n=38 Verbel 2026-09-28 XL+Block-Wiedemann; Type V n=31 Li-Sun 2026-09-17 'Improved F4 via smaller matrices' on 2x RTX 5090; Type VI n=36 Sakata-Takagi 2025-10-16 HDF4+MF4)
papers.authors: Javier Verbel; Ting Li, Yao Sun; Kosuke Sakata, Tsuyoshi Takagi
papers.venue: mqchallenge.org hall of fame and detail pages
papers.summary: Type II (GF(256), m=2n): n=38 solved by XL with block Wiedemann in 811,805 s (BW1 684,568 s) on 2x EPYC 7763 with 1 TB RAM. Type V (GF(256), n~1.5m): n=31,m=21 solved by a modified F4 building more compact matrices, fixing 11 variables, 80 subsystem instances at ~9,027 s each on 2 GPUs + 16 threads (total 8d 8h); no paper yet ('future paper'). Type VI (GF(31)): n=36, m=24 solved in ~11.5 days on 4x EPYC 7763 by HDF4+MF4, guessing 15 variables, 2,011 instances. No new Type I/III/IV (GF(2)) records in 2025-2026: the Boolean square record remains Bouillaguet-Sauvage n=76 (2023-06, Crossbred-type, 20,480 cores) and Type IV n=114 (2024-07).
papers.relevance: Lever 1: Boolean (Type I) records have stalled at n=76 since 2023, i.e. the practical ceiling for dense random Boolean MQ at degree-of-regularity ~? is unchanged; the programme's descended S_4 cells with ~130-200 Boolean variables remain far beyond generic solving, so any progress must come from structure (growth or non-growth of d_F), not from solver records. Lever 5: Li-Sun's 'smaller matrices' F4 on GPUs is unpublished; if it is a block/structured matrix construction it overlaps with equivariant blocks. Engineering class.
papers.suggested_route: Watch item: fetch the Li-Sun paper when it appears; otherwise none (records are generic-system engineering).

papers.title: A decrementally-improved algorithm for Boolean MQ
papers.summary: Combines the Lokshtanov-Paturi-Tamaki-Williams-Yu polynomial method with Dinur's second algorithm (EUROCRYPT 2021), stripping some of its machinery; 1-4 bit improvement for MQOM parameters; shows PGOW-MQ (partial-guessing one-wayness) is 2-4x easier than MQ, giving MQOM attacks 3-4 bits below claimed level with huge memory; surveys UOV-shape changes of variables (improving Thomae-Wolf and Furue-Nakamura-Takagi for underdetermined Boolean systems) and solves the largest underdetermined Fukuoka challenges with a matrix-pencil technique. Reports estimates Crossbred 144 vs Dinur-2 142 bits at level I.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none (generic Boolean MQ; exponent class unchanged, ~0.69n). Confirms the treatise's accounting that Crossbred/Dinur are engineering relative to the descended-system exponent. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: None for the exponent; optional pricing update of the Boolean oracle cost table (Crossbred 0.891 bit-op exponent vs Dinur-2) in the Koblitz cost model.

papers.title: Improved preprocessing for the Crossbred algorithm and application to the MQ problem
papers.authors: Damien Vidal, Claire Delaplace, Sorina Ionica
papers.summary: Corrects omissions in the Crossbred complexity analysis, gives a complete analysis, and a criterion that reduces the number of polynomials generated in preprocessing for admissible (D,d,k); applied to MQOM. Ionica is a WDSat co-author; the paper does not mention Weil descent or ECDLP.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none. Confirms no WDSat/Weil-descent follow-up from the WDSat group in 2026 (their current line is Crossbred/MQOM). Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Polynomial Evaluation on Many Inputs with Bounded Hamming Weight over GF(2) (ePrint 2026/040) and Derivative-Based Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials over Product Hamming Balls (ePrint 2026/197)
papers.authors: Fukang Liu, Vaibhav Dixit, Muzhou Li, Daisuke Yamamoto, Wakaha Ogata, Santanu Sarkar, Willi Meier; Vaibhav Dixit, Santanu Sarkar, Fukang Liu, Willi Meier
papers.summary: FESG: fast exhaustive evaluation of a degree-d Boolean polynomial over products of bounded-Hamming-weight sets in binom(n,<=d) + d|P| bit operations and 2 binom(n,<=d) bits of memory, with initialisation cut from O(binom(n,<=d)^2) to O(binom(n,<=d)); supplies the previously unproven subroutine of Dinur's polynomial method without changing its complexity. 2026/197 generalises to F_q and F_{q^rho} with O(d|B|) evaluation over product Hamming balls and memory independent of the number of points.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none. Lever 6/8 (flagged, not this lane): fast evaluation over Hamming balls is exactly the primitive a Hamming-ball factor base oracle (enumerate low-weight x and test membership) would use; makes the 'x-functional filter' over low-weight sets cheap. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Hand to the factor-base lane: price an enumeration oracle for a weight-<=w base over F_{2^131} using FESG costs vs the subspace F4 oracle at matched base size.

papers.title: XL engineering 2026: A Memory-efficient Implementation of Wiedemann XL (ePrint 2026/2641); Concrete Bit-Operation Cost of XL (ePrint 2026/1382); A Practical Optimization for Wiedemann XL (2026/1787); On Memory Effects in PWXL variants (2026/1819)
papers.authors: Daniel Cabarcas, Tung Chou, Felipe Merino, Javier Verbel; Hülya Evkan, Ruben Niederhagen; Tung Chou, Ruben Niederhagen; Jintai Ding, Hao Guo, Bo-Yin Yang
papers.summary: 2026/2641: first efficient on-the-fly Wiedemann-XL (rows of the Macaulay matrix regenerated during BW1, column indices in O(n^2) look-ups), up to 5x less memory at comparable time, F_2/F_16/F_31 (SSE) and F_256 (AVX2). 2026/1382: CryptAttackTester-style closed-form bit-operation costs for XL + Wiedemann + Berlekamp-Massey over GF(2), GF(31), GF(256), validated on circuits, applied to Fukuoka and NIST candidates. 2026/1787 and 2026/1819 (abstracts not opened) are further XL/PWXL memory optimisations.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none. Lever 5: the on-the-fly Macaulay row generation is the memory model an equivariant XL/F4 over F_{2^130} would need (character blocks are too large to store densely); the bit-operation cost model gives a published, auditable pricing for the programme's Boolean XL stage. Engineering class.
papers.suggested_route: Accounting: re-price the programme's descended S_4 Macaulay stages at (m,l)=(4,4),(4,5),(4,6) in the Evkan-Niederhagen bit-operation model to obtain a published-cost-model baseline before claiming any equivariant speedup.

papers.title: Attacking UOV-based Signatures with Schur--Macaulay Matrices (and: Extending the Schur--Macaulay Framework for UOV Attacks via Truncated Polynomial Algebras, ePrint 2026/2444)
papers.authors: Simon-Philipp Merz, Lars Ran; Peigen Li, Siyong Tao
papers.summary: In characteristic 2, 'divided powers' of alternating polar forms give new equations vanishing on the oil space not implied by the originals (a tower of such equations); Macaulay matrices are generalised to arbitrary Schur-module shapes lambda (symmetric and exterior powers as extremes), with conjectured, experimentally confirmed Hilbert series; breaks several Round-2 MAYO/SNOVA parameter sets. 2026/2444 extends via truncated polynomial algebras.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: a new characteristic-2-specific source of extra low-degree equations (divided powers, i.e. the integer lift of x^2 = 2*x^{(2)}) that are invisible to the ideal over F_2 -- structurally the same phenomenon as the trace linear equation that forces d_ff = 2 for S_3; worth asking whether descended S_{m+1} systems admit divided-power equations beyond the field equations. Lever 5: Schur-Macaulay matrices are a representation-theoretic refinement of the Macaulay matrix; the Frobenius-character decomposition of the barrel system is a different (abelian) representation theory but the 'Hilbert series per isotypic piece' methodology is the same.
papers.suggested_route: Theory probe: lift the descended S_3 system to Z/4 or Z[x] (Witt-vector/Teichmüller lift of the normal-basis coordinates), square and divide by 2, reduce mod 2; check whether the resulting polynomials lie in the F_2-ideal generated by the system plus field equations at n=13..21. If not, they are new equations lowering d_F (an 'advance' candidate in the solving stage); if always in the ideal, record the obstruction.

papers.title: Extending CDCL to disjunctions of parity equations (Xorcle)
papers.summary: CDCL(+): CDCL generalised to XNF formulas (clauses that are disjunctions of parity equations); produces Res(+) proofs and polynomially simulates Res(+) given nondeterministic decisions/restarts; new Res(+) inference rules allow 1-UIP learning; Xorcle prototype with LRUP(+) proof logging beats Kissat, CryptoMiniSat 5.13 and 2-Xornado on native XNF benchmarks; near-polynomial scaling on Tseitin formulas.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: SAT solvers are enumerators on PDP (treatise prog_binary.tex: 'SAT, SMT and WDSat are enumerators'); a Res(+)-complete learner does not change that unless the descended system has short Res(+) refutations, which is unknown. Lever 5: none. Relevant to LEAD-ICE-sat-xor-pdp-oracle and LEAD-ICP-icperf-binary-pdp-solver as the strongest 2026 XOR-native solver.
papers.suggested_route: Experiment (toy): encode the 60 published Trimoska S_4 instances and programme instances at n=17..25 in XNF (x_i^2 = x_i, descended equations as XOR-rich clauses), run Xorcle vs WDSat vs CryptoMiniSat; the question is whether UNSAT (non-decomposable R) instances show Res(+) proof size growing slower than 2^l. Honest pricing per BRIEF rule 5.

papers.title: Conflict-Driven SAT Solving using XOR-OR-AND Normal Forms (Xorricane)
papers.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 86 (2026), DOI 10.1613/jair.1.20298
papers.summary: XLIN proof system for XNF shown polynomially equivalent to Res(+) and SRES (exponential separation from resolution); CDXCL conflict-driven framework with Gaussian constraint propagation; Xorricane implementation with lazy data structures matches or beats CNF and CNF-XOR solvers on XOR-rich (cryptographic) instances. Builds on Andraschko-Danner-Kreuzer's 2-XNF/2-Xornado (arXiv 2311.00733) which converts ANF Boolean polynomials to 2-XNF.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: same enumerator caveat; however ANF-to-XNF conversion is the natural input path for the descended Semaev ANF. Note the KB already holds a CoDIT 2025 paper 'ANF-Based Satisfiability for Weil-Descent Cryptographic Attacks' (KN-LIT-92919e) from this circle, so the XNF-on-Weil-descent idea is known to the programme. Lever 5: none.
papers.novelty_note: The JAIR 2026 Xorricane article is not carded; the related CoDIT 2025 Weil-descent ANF-SAT paper is (KN-LIT-92919e).
papers.suggested_route: Fold into the Xorcle experiment above as a second XNF solver.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Open-Source Gröbner Basis Implementations for Small-Scale AES Polynomial Systems over GF(2)
papers.summary: Benchmarks 20 open-source Groebner implementations against Magma on small-scale AES systems over GF(2) with field equations (Easy/Medium/Hard, 10 instances each). Hard: msolve 164 s mean (13.4 cores, 3.7 GiB), Singular slimgb 269 s, Magma 319 s (16.9 GiB). Ranking depends on the instance.
papers.relevance: Lever 1/5: engineering baseline confirming msolve as the best open F4 over GF(2) with field equations in 2026, i.e. the right reference solver for the programme's unmeasured cells; also confirms open tools are not an order of magnitude behind Magma (relevant to BRIEF closure 'Frontier measurement' audits).
papers.suggested_route: None beyond citing it as the solver-parity reference for 'f4_fp at msolve parity' claims.

papers.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: Deterministic univariate root finding over F_q using the groups E(F_q) and its quadratic twist instead of F_q^*: an offline field-only datum D (certifiable deterministically in time poly(log q, Xi(D)), Xi = largest prime factor of |E||E~|) and an online deterministic phase in O~(Xi(D)^2 n log^2 q + n^omega log q + n log^3 q); conjecture that large-characteristic fields admit Xi(D) <= (log q)^{O(1)}.
papers.relevance: Out of lane but flagged for open lever 2 (root finding beyond two summands on prime curves): it is the reverse direction (elliptic curves helping root finding), not root finding helping ECDLP, and gives no sub-N^2 structure for S_4 membership; included because it is the only Oct-2026 cs.SC paper linking elliptic-curve groups to polynomial solving. Lever 1/5: none.
papers.suggested_route: None for IC; note as 'reverse-direction' literature in the lever-2 file.

papers.title: Beyond F5 and GVW: The Proper-Cover Algorithm for Fast Ideal Basis Computation
papers.authors: Sheng-Ming Ma, Yi Liu, Zheng-Lin Jiao
papers.summary: Signature-based 'Proper-Cover' algorithm for zero-dimensional ideals combining GVW cover optimisation with proper-basis (parameterised coefficient) theory; proves termination/correctness; claims to beat F5 under all orders and GVW under lex; no benchmark names or factors in the abstract.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: signature-based solvers expose the syzygy cascade (LEAD-ICE-syzygy-cascade-signatures); a faster signature engine is only engineering. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Low priority; if an implementation appears, run it on the descended S_3 instances to count non-rewritable syzygies by degree (the syzygy-cascade lead).

papers.title: A data structure for monomial ideals with applications to signature Gröbner bases
papers.authors: Pierre Lairez, Rafael Mohr, Théo Ternier
papers.summary: Monomial divisibility diagrams (shared-subtree DAG) for monomial ideals with fast membership and insertion; integrated into AlgebraicSolving.jl's signature Groebner basis to detect reductions to zero; 'substantial speed-ups' over divmask generator lists.
papers.relevance: Lever 5: engineering for signature-based F5-type runs; a Frobenius-equivariant variant would need orbit-closed monomial ideals, which MDDs could represent compactly. Lever 1: none.
papers.suggested_route: None now.

papers.title: Learning Fast Monomial Orders for Gröbner Basis Computations; HATSolver: Learning Gröbner Bases with Hierarchical Attention Transformers (ICLR 2026)

papers.summary: Bunch et al.: monomial-order selection as reinforcement learning with Monte-Carlo cost estimates; learned policies beat grevlex-style heuristics on systems-biology and vision benchmarks and resist distillation into simple rules. HATSolver: tree-structured attention transformer predicting Groebner bases, scaling beyond Kera-Ishihara (NeurIPS 2024) with curriculum learning.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: none directly; the programme's own result that d_F depends on the presentation (monomial order / coordinates) is exactly what a learned order selector would exploit, so a learned-order experiment on descended S_3 is a cheap test of 'presentation slack' (LEAD-ICE-curve-presentation-invariance). ML lever 12 adjacency. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Toy: random-search (not RL) over 200 degree-compatible weight orders for descended S_3 at n=17, l=4; record min/median closure degree; if min < measured d_F under grevlex, presentation slack exists and lever 1 must be stated per order.

papers.title: Computability of Equivariant Gröbner bases
papers.summary: For a group G acting on an infinite set of indeterminates, equivariant Groebner bases are computable (and equivariant membership decidable) when the Hilbert basis property holds; sufficient condition for undecidability otherwise. Infinite-variable setting.
papers.relevance: Lever 5: NEGATIVE relevance recorded for completeness: the 2024-2026 'equivariant Groebner basis' literature (Hillar-Krone-Leykin lineage) is about infinitely many variables and decidability, not about speeding up F4 under a finite Frobenius action over F_2. The only finite-group computational lineage remains Faugère-Svartz 2012/2013 (abelian, non-modular) and Steidel 2012; none handles the modular case (|G| = n = 131 is odd so char 2 is non-modular -- Faugère-Svartz's diagonalisation applies over F_{2^130} as the treatise already states). No 2024-2026 successor found. Lever 1: none.
papers.suggested_route: None; documents that lever 5 has no external shortcut.

papers.title: Algebraic Modelings of the Supersingular Isogeny Problem
papers.authors: Alessio Caminata, Andrea Sanguineti, Silvia Sconza
papers.summary: Polynomial systems for 2^k/3^k-isogeny paths from Renes formulas (Montgomery/triangular forms); proves zero-dimensionality, computes dim of the top-degree part, shows the systems are NOT in generic coordinates; Groebner solving much faster than modular-polynomial modeling.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: a worked example of Caminata's own framework meeting a structured elliptic-curve system that is not in generic coordinates -- the same situation the programme expects for descended Semaev systems; their method for computing dim F^top is reusable. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: Reuse their dim(F^top) computation as the generic-coordinates test for descended S_{m+1}.

papers.title: A New Algebraic Algorithm for LWE

papers.summary: Search-LWE algorithm combining linear algebra with S-polynomial steps; direct complexity analysis without semi-regularity or degree-of-regularity assumptions; claims a polynomial improvement over prior Groebner-based LWE solvers.
papers.relevance: Lever 1: methodological interest only (a direct, assumption-free complexity analysis of a structured system of the Arora-Ge type); shows the community is moving away from semi-regularity heuristics toward provable per-system analyses, which is the lever-1 programme's own stance. Lever 5: none.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: msolve releases v0.9.0-v0.11.0 (improved Gebauer-Möller in F4, tier policy, probabilistic linear algebra and Hankel inversion fixes, lower memory for GB over QQ, global seed)
